column2: How do I animate a map or a chart through time (Animation studio)?
column3: Editing tools → “🎞 Animation studio”, or “🎞 Animate” under a dated diagram. A film is made of scenes (title, diagram, family migrations, name race, living pyramid, self-drawing curve, growing tree, changing borders) laid out on a timeline: the camera, captions, music and your voice are set scene by scene. “⤓ Export” makes a video (WebM or MP4), a GIF, images or subtitles; “🎬 Continue in Video editing” sends the film to editing.

column2: How do I show France’s borders changing over time?
column3: Animation studio → “🏛 Changing borders” template (or “＋ Scene” → “The changing borders”): France from 1760 to today, year by year (Lorraine, Corsica, Revolution and Empire, 1815, Savoy and Nice in 1860, Alsace-Moselle from 1871 to 1918), with the dates that matter. Settings: framing, colours, years. These are approximate borders, drawn from today’s boundaries.

column2: Can the app suggest the right diagram for me (“I want to show…”)?
column3: Yes: in “New diagram”, write what you want to show (“the most common first names”, “where people came from”…) then “Guess”. The app suggests three diagrams made from your database, the best suited first; “Make this diagram” opens it in the editor.

column2: Can my statistics palette have more than 40 colours?
column3: Yes: Charts → 🎨 Stats and tree colours. The palette has 100 colours, all different; “＋ 10 colours” adds some (up to 400), “− 10 colours” removes some (“↶ Undo” puts them back). The cycle starts again after the last colour.

column2: Which box designs are there for trees?
column3: Charts → 🎨 Stats and tree colours → “🌳 Tree boxes”: 14 boxes to choose from (white, man / woman colours, with photo, mini, parchment, medallion, shield, postcard, postage stamp, polaroid, museum label, pastel by generation, outline only, golden night), then the width, lines, dates and Sosa number.

column2: How do I follow the law of the time, the taxes and the heirs of an estate?
column3: In an estate file, “⚖️ Law and shares” tab: the law in force at the time of death (before or after 2002, 1972…), parentage, successive estates (an heir who died after the deceased), the matrimonial property regime, the will and gifts (reserved portion, disposable portion), an estimate of the inheritance tax and deadlines, and a deceased person with ties abroad. Amounts are never kept. The “🗂 Heir tracking” tab sorts each heir by stage, with their sources and next follow-up.

column2: How do I open an estate file step by step?
column3: Estates → “🧭 Step by step”: 1. the deceased person (the file opens, “↶ Undo” deletes it), 2. the family found, 3. the doubts (alive at the death or not, one click), 4. the heirs and their shares.

column2: How do I compare my calculation with the notary’s deed of notoriety?
column3: “⚖️ Law and shares” tab → “📄 Compare with the deed of notoriety”: paste the list of heirs from the deed (one per line, with their share: “1/4”, “25 %”, “half”). The app says for each one “same”, “different” or “not in the deed”, and shows those in the deed it didn’t find.

column2: How do I add my own base map?
column3: Settings → Maps → Map backgrounds → “🗺 ＋ Add a base map”: a name and the tile address (https://…/{z}/{x}/{y}.png; {s} for subdomains, {-y} for the TMS format), from a site that allows it without a key. “👁 Try” shows a tile; the base map appears in “My base maps” in every menu. An address with a key is refused (it would be readable in plain text).

column2: How do I keep several readings of a record and take the best of each?
column3: In the Transcription workshop, each reading (handwriting, printed text, in-depth AI reading) is kept on its own in 🕘 Versions, without overwriting the others. File → “⚖️ Compare readings…”: the passages that differ, word by word or line by line; one click picks a variant, “the majority” takes what most readings say, then “Put into the text” (↶ Undo).

column2: How do I tell automatic reading to skip part of the image (a “do not read” zone)?
column3: In the Workshop, draw a zone (▭), then in its bar choose its kind: “⛔ Do not read” (a stamp, a seal), or marginal note, title, signatures, added note. Lines in a ⛔ zone are skipped by automatic reading and exports; the other kinds set the reading order.

column2: How do I export a transcription as ALTO or PAGE (Transkribus, eScriptorium)?
column3: Workshop → Export: “🧾 ALTO” (lines and words with their position on the image, the format used by libraries and archives) or “📄 PAGE” (regions, lines, reading order; one file per page, as a .zip if there are several). TEI is still there too.

column2: How do I transcribe a page of a collection in the Workshop?
column3: On the collection page: “📜 Open in the Transcription Workshop”. The Workshop opens on its photo (the transcription already started, otherwise a new one); when you come back, if the page was empty, its text is put in (↶ Undo).

column2: How do I create a collection from an online register (IIIF)?
column3: Lists → Collections → “⋯” → “🌐 From an online register…”: paste the address of the IIIF manifest (often …/manifest.json, sometimes behind an IIIF logo) from the archive, the library or Gallica. The app gives its title and number of images; choose all the images or from… to…, then “Download”: each image becomes a page of a new collection (“Stop” keeps what is done; ↶ Undo deletes the collection).

column2: How do I spot blank pages and photos taken twice in a collection?
column3: Collection → 🗂 Status tab → “🔍 Blank pages and duplicates”: the app looks at each photo and suggests the pages that seem blank and the photos that look alike. Nothing changes without “Do what is ticked”; the removed photo stays in Media, and “↶ Undo” puts everything back.

column2: How do I see my documents on a map or on a timeline?
column3: Documents, on the right: “🗺 Map” (one circle per place, a click shows its documents) or “📅 Timeline” (documents sorted by decade), next to “▦ Thumbnails”. The choice is remembered; it follows the filters in the left column.
